---
title: "MetaChoice: Generating MultiChoice Variants"
page-layout: article
---

This guide explains how to generate multiple-choice questions (MCQs) from a shared pool of choices using MetaChoice. You can define global and per-stem constraints, mark correct choices by keys, and generate one or multiple combinations per stem.

Key ideas:
- Use Choice(key, text) to register choices with a short identifier and a long display text.
- Group constraints operate on keys.
- Stems have required keys and texts; you can add per-stem groups and mark correct choices.
- Generation samples subsets of size n that satisfy all constraints; you may generate multiple variants per stem (limit).

## Quick start

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.meta import MetaChoice, Stem, Choice, Constraint

mc = (
    MetaChoice()
    .set_choices([
        Choice("T1", "President T1"),
        Choice("T2", "President T2"),
        Choice("P1", "Policy P1"),
        Choice("P2", "Policy P2"),
        Choice("A1", "Attractor A1"),
    ])
    .add_constraint(Constraint("term", choices={"T1", "T2"}, min=1, max=1))
    .add_constraint(Constraint("policy", choices={"P1", "P2"}, min=0, max=1))
)

mc.add_stem(Stem("TERM_Q", "Who served two terms?").set_choices_correct({"T1", "T2"}))
mc.add_stem(Stem("TERM_POLICY_Q", "Pick a term and a policy").set_choices_correct({"T1", "T2"}).add_constraint(Constraint("policy", choices={"P1","P2"}, min=1, max=1)))

group = mc.generate_multichoice(n=3, limit=2, seed=42)
# Combine with a Quiz
from questionsafe.quiz import Quiz
Quiz(category="Demo").add_group(group)
# Peek at first two variants
group.variants[0], group.variants[1]
```

## Shorthand inputs for choices

Preferred: Choice objects. Shorthand coercions are supported for convenience:

- Dict mapping: {"id": "long text", ...}
- Strings with a colon: "id: long text" (first colon splits). If no colon, the same string is used as both key and text.

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.meta import MetaChoice
mc = MetaChoice()
mc.set_choices({"X": "Long X", "Y": "Long Y"})
mc.add_choices(["Z: Long Z", "W"])  # W -> key==text
list(mc._choices.keys())
```

Duplicate keys raise ValueError in set_choices/add_choices/add_choice.

## Stems and correctness

Define per-stem constraints and correct groups by keys. Correctness is just another group—MetaChoice uses an internal reserved id ("__correct__").

```{python}
#| echo: true
from questionsafe.meta import MetaChoice, Stem, Choice, Constraint
mc = MetaChoice().set_choices(["A", "B", "C"])  # shorthand key==text
s = Stem("S1", "Pick A and one more").set_group_correct({"A"})
mc.add_stem(s)
group = mc.generate_multichoice(n=2, limit=1, seed=1)
[a.text for a in group.variants[0].answers]
```

## Generation controls

- n: number of choices per generated MCQ, uniform across stems.
- limit: maximum number of distinct combinations per stem; total MCQs <= (#stems × limit), capped by feasibility.
- seed: base seed; per-stem seeds are derived deterministically (seed + index).
- randomize_order / randomize_branch: control randomness in the sampler.

Answers are always listed in the registered pool order for stability.

## Design notes

- Choice keys decouple identifiers from long texts, allowing stable grouping and constraints.
- All groups operate on keys; the sampler never touches raw text—only keys.
- MultiChoice answers are materialized from keys by looking up the registered Choice text; uniform fractions (100/k) are assigned to the k correct items in each variant.
